evidence: src/business/logic/BoxOffice.ts: constructor injects `EventStore` and `TicketStore` and works on domain types `Event` and `Ticket` (e.g. `event.sell(seats)`, `ticket.admit(new Date())`).

src/business/logic/GateLog.ts: constructor injects `PrismaService` and calls `this.prisma.scan.create({ data: { id: `${gate}:${code}`, code, gate, at: new Date() } })` and `this.prisma.scan.findMany()` directly, with no store and no domain type.
src/business/logic/BoxOffice.ts admit(): `await this.tickets.markScanned(ticket.code, ticket.scannedAt ?? new Date())` records the scan in the ticket store.
src/business/logic/GateLog.ts scanned(code, gate): keeps a separate scan record with its own `new Date()` timestamp, not linked to Ticket.admit or markScanned.
src/business/logic/BoxOffice.ts: `new Event(data.id, data.title, data.venueCapacity, data.seatsSold, data.startsAt, data.priceCents)` appears in both purchase() and listing().
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The two files don't share one abstraction or boundary. BoxOffice works through the store abstractions (EventStore, TicketStore). It turns their rows into the domain types Event and Ticket and leaves rules like sell() and admit() to them. GateLog skips all of that: it writes to and reads from the raw `prisma.scan` model through PrismaService, with no store and no domain type. The two files also both cover ticket scanning but are not linked. BoxOffice.admit records the scan with tickets.markScanned(). GateLog.scanned keeps a separate scan record, keyed by gate:code, with its own timestamp. So the 'ticket scanned' fact is stored in two places and nothing keeps them consistent. A third, smaller issue sits inside BoxOffice: the code that builds an Event from a store row appears twice, in purchase() and in listing(). Import direction is out of scope and was not judged. This finding is about mixed abstractions and a rule stored twice.

violations.message: Skips the module's store/domain abstraction. It talks to PrismaService (`prisma.scan.create`, `prisma.scan.findMany`) directly, while BoxOffice works through EventStore/TicketStore and the Ticket/Event domain types.

Records ticket scans a second time. `scanned(code, gate)` writes its own scan record and timestamp, separate from BoxOffice.admit → Ticket.admit → tickets.markScanned, so the 'ticket scanned' fact lives in two places that aren't kept consistent.

The code that builds an Event from a store row (`new Event(d.id, d.title, d.venueCapacity, d.seatsSold, d.startsAt, d.priceCents)`) is written out in both purchase() and listing() instead of in one place.
